text: • Guest simulator data: practice cash, positions and trade history are stored in your browser with a separate browser-local recovery copy. You can download or explicitly restore a portable practice backup JSON file containing trading history and any private journal notes. The backup feature does not upload this file. Backup formats can be manually edited: TradeHQ validates file structure and arithmetic but does not certify authenticity, investment performance or leaderboard ranking. An imported guest file remains unverified. Guest learning-journey progress, course progress, streaks and related settings remain browser-stored. For signed-in users, lesson completion, unfinished quiz answers, reading position and first-trade journey progress may also be saved privately in Supabase and synchronized across devices when online. New beginner-journey reflection text stays on the device. Older reflections already synchronized remain private in the account. Streaks and unrelated browser preferences are not part of this account sync. • Signed-in portfolio data: Supabase stores account cash, positions and server-recorded practice orders, including asset, quantity, execution price, fees, time and simulated result. These account records restore across devices when the service is available. Signed-in users can also download a server-signed current-cycle historical practice export and verify its integrity against their authenticated account. This file may contain account identifiers and private transaction details; it is not publicly shared or accepted as an upload that replaces ranked trades. A first-time browser import stores cash and positions as an unranked portfolio; earlier guest trade history stays in its original browser. Starting a fresh ranked practice cycle archives the previous account snapshot privately. Journals remain browser-held; signed-in lesson and beginner-journey progress can sync privately and are not used to determine public trading ranks. • Optional account data: if you create an account, Supabase processes authentication data such as your email or provider identity and can store profile fields including username, country and bio. • Community data: signed-in features can store selected practice statistics, public-profile settings, reviews and duel/challenge records. A separate setting, OFF by default, lets a member voluntarily disclose up to 20 current-cycle server-recorded simulated trade entries on an otherwise public profile: asset, buy/sell, quantity, execution price, fee and date. The public data response also includes trade total, simulated realised profit/loss where recorded, and price-source information, even when a visible profile row shows fewer fields. Private journals, reflections, past cycles and browser-only records are never shared by this feature. These are simulated results, not brokerage statements or verified real-money performance. • Review interactions: likes are stored with your account ID and the review ID to enforce one like per account. Public pages show totals, not individual liker identities. Owner replies are public. Reviews removed from public view remain in the private admin panel for restoration. • Optional TradeHQ Newsletter: if you explicitly request the educational newsletter, TradeHQ stores your email address, consent/confirmation status, the date and source of signup, unsubscribe status, and delivery receipts in private Supabase records. Resend handles email delivery and receives your address for confirmations and issues. We never add prior contact records to the mailing list without permission. Every newsletter provides an unsubscribe link, and you may use the contact page to request deletion. • Contact messages: by default the contact page opens your email app or lets you copy a draft into webmail. If the optional direct-send service is configured, Cloudflare Turnstile processes challenge and connection information and Resend processes the message, sender reply address and recipient information to deliver it to the maintainer's inbox. TradeHQ does not retain direct-send message bodies in its application database. The maintainer's email provider retains delivered messages according to its settings. • Technical data: hosting, authentication, security and abuse-prevention services can receive normal request information such as IP address, browser/device information and server logs. • Website performance: current pages load Cloudflare Web Analytics to measure page loading and performance. Its browser beacon can send the page URL, a page-load identifier, timing and browser performance measurements to Cloudflare, separately from optional Amplitude events. These performance requests can run before an analytics choice and after Amplitude is rejected. Cloudflare states that its Web Analytics usage metrics do not use cookies, local storage or fingerprinting to track individuals. This does not mean that network requests contain no connection information or that every jurisdiction exempts this processing from privacy requirements. • Font delivery: pages request stylesheets and font files from Google Fonts. Google receives the connecting IP address, the requested resource URL and request headers, which can include browser/operating-system information and the referring page according to browser settings. These requests are separate from Amplitude consent and may occur before a choice or after rejection. Google states that its Fonts API does not set or log cookies and does not use Fonts information to create end-user profiles or for targeted advertising. • Optional analytics and advertising data: TradeHQ offers a newly scoped analytics choice only to visitors affirmatively confirming they are at least 18. This confirmation is for optional analytics; it is not an age restriction on lessons, guest practice or sign-in. Visitors under 18 should reject optional analytics. If accepted, Amplitude can receive limited Practice Arena milestone events and two leaderboard registration-flow events (an eligible signed-out leaderboard visit, and a newly created account subsequently authenticated in that same browser within seven days), along with its pseudonymous browser identity and ordinary network metadata. The two leaderboard custom events contain no email, account ID, username, profile details, portfolio data, transaction information, or form content. The temporary seven-day same-browser attribution marker stores only a visit timestamp and is cleared on consent rejection or successful attribution. No custom Amplitude events are sent when optional analytics is declined; the website does not claim visitor identity is anonymous. Amplitude's automatic page, click, form, network and attribution collection and session replay are disabled; the two explicitly triggered attribution events are the only leaderboard funnel measurement. Earlier v1/v2 analytics permissions are not reused. Google AdSense has separate advertising choices and may use cookies or similar identifiers for ad delivery, measurement and, where applicable, personalisation. • Practice Arena research: exercise decisions, private written reasons, closing reflections and history stay in your browser and are not automatically submitted to a research database. An optional, adult-only research questionnaire keeps answers on the open page and only prepares an email if you deliberately choose to do so; you must send that email yourself. Sending an email reveals your sender address and may include other email-provider metadata. Answers are not anonymous once linked with a sender or identifying comments. If you accept Amplitude analytics, TradeHQ may record Arena view/start/finish/resume milestones, scenario ID and difficulty, and whether this browser returned on a later day. Custom Arena events do not include trading choices, portfolio values, account IDs, written notes or questionnaire answers. This opt-in measurement uses the existing Amplitude service's consented visitor identity; it does not create a separate TradeHQ research identifier. Declining analytics disables those custom milestones. A same-browser return event does not prove a person learned or voluntarily returned.

text: Ad-serving scripts and placements are currently disabled on TradeHQ, including newly published courses, account pages and error screens. The publisher verification meta tag and ads.txt do not enable ad serving. Before advertising can be enabled, TradeHQ must verify Google site approval, suitable reviewed inventory, placement controls and applicable consent configuration. If advertising is enabled, Google and its partners may place or read cookies and use similar technologies, web beacons, IP addresses and other identifiers to deliver and measure ads. Third parties may collect information as a result of ad serving. Advertising cookies can reflect prior visits to TradeHQ or other sites and, where consent and law permit, support personalised ads. These uses remain subject to the applicable privacy choices. Advertising may be personalized, non-personalized or limited depending on consent, location and Google settings.

text: Trophy display is disabled by default even for a public trader profile, including older profiles that were historically public by default. After an account is confirmed and its profile is deliberately public, the owner may separately enable display of one earned trophy flair and up to three earned pinned trophies. Only the chosen trophy names/icons are shown publicly; scores, assessment dates, balances, trades, contacts and private learning history are not included. You may withdraw this permission in My Trophy Cabinet, or hide the entire profile; both actions stop the optional trophy display.

text: The optional leaderboard attribution marker contains only a local visit timestamp and is eligible for matching for no more than seven days. If the person does not return, the expired timestamp may remain in browser storage until the next relevant page access, consent withdrawal or site-data clearing; it is then discarded or replaced. A successful attributed registration also clears the marker. Analytics and advertising data at external providers are retained according to their settings and policies; TradeHQ does not state a fixed provider retention period where it cannot verify one.
